**Synopsis:**
The article argues that the August CPI print (due Sept 10) has become the pivotal swing factor for a Fed rate hike at the Sept 15–16 FOMC meeting — an outsized role for a single data point, especially given Fed Chair Warsh's own stated preference for trend-based policy. The piece highlights a communications vacuum under Warsh, Governor Waller's conditional hawkish signaling, and a bond market rout as the backdrop. Rates markets are pricing a 65% probability of a hike. The author questions whether rounding differences at the third decimal place of core CPI are a rational basis for the world's most consequential monetary policy decision.

The only offset is residual uncertainty around the exact CPI print and Warsh's communications ambiguity.)
